title: close silently leaves console descriptors open
description:
The syscall bridge reports a successful close without closing the descriptor, so defined C code produces a different result and an extra console effect (P0 wrong result/silent fallback).

Input: close(1); errno=0; n=write(1,"X",1). Expected: n=-1, errno=EBADF, no output. Actual: n=1, console byte X; repeated close(1) also returns success. An independent native build of the same unmodified C source returns status 0/empty stdout, while the published checked runtime returns status 71/stdout X, on LLVM 18 and 23. title: Native checker under-publishes accepted one-lane i64 vector
description:
Oracle. scripts/native-check.cpp:108,143-146 assumes every fixed vector <=128 bits takes an SSE register. Accepted <1 x i64> is stack-passed by both native LLVM18/23 backends even with SSE registers free. title: native-check classifier counts register-passed __float128 variadic operands as 16 stack bytes (oracle: wrong verdict both directions)
description: scripts/native-check.cpp:123 classifies FP128 like X86_FP80: unconditional memory(16,16). On x86-64 SysV __float128 is SSE class: one xmm slot when available (caller asm: movaps into %xmm0, %al=1), 16-byte stack slot only when SSE exhausted. Published overflow extents are therefore wrong whenever an fp128 operand is register-passed. Repro at 642c53c on LLVM 18 and 23 (probes in bennett-runtimes-pa-muse/.tmp/rev-pa-muse-landing-muse/{abi-extra,fp128-probe,fp128-boundary,fp128-named}.py, run via .tmp/pa/in-slot.sh 1800): (1) take(0,2.0Q,1,2,3,4,5,6) has one true 8-byte overflow slot but va_push(24); a 7th and 8th va_arg(int) read are accepted (exit 0), 9th faults 7 at +24; gp-only control publishes 8 and faults 7, long-double control publishes 24 and faults 7 (fp80 is MEMORY class). (2) Named take(int,__float128,double x8,...) reading a variadic 16-byte vector publishes 16 but the true suffix is 24: valid program plain=0, checked faults 7. (3) Spilled fp128 (after 8 doubles) publishes 16 and passes. Fix: classify FP128 like a 128-bit SSE vector (sse<8 ? ++sse : memory(16,16)); add fp128 register/spill/named cases to tests/test_native_checked_varargs.py. Same determining shape as brt-zni (P1 oracle). Review: docs/reviews/2026-11-08-pa-muse-landing-muse.md P1-1.
